name: Richardson
seo_title: Richardson, TX Christmas Events for Kids 2026: 6 Events
seo_description: Richardson kids' Christmas: free Santa's Village at Huffhines Park, the Christmas Parade and four Nutcracker and holiday ballets at the Eisemann Center.
lede: The story of Christmas in Richardson is the story of Santa's Village, which the city began hosting in 1989 beside City Hall and which now fills Huffhines Park with 13 North Pole dwellings, plus an annual Christmas Parade and a December of ballets at the Eisemann Center. Richardson's 2026 season counts 6 events, led by Santa's Village on December 5 to 6, 11 to 13 and 18 to 20.
sections: In 1989 the City of Richardson began hosting a seasonal Santa's Village next to its new city hall, according to the Handbook of Texas. The city's own history page says the first village was one continuous row of charming dwellings arranged in an L shape. In 1996 Alcatel committed $125,000 over five years to improve it, which added 16 larger stand-alone dwellings, fencing and festive lighting. After a fire at Richardson City Hall, the village moved to Huffhines Park, 1500 Apollo Road, where families now walk through it for free.
Thirteen dwellings, one tiny North Pole

Local groups run the dwellings, and kids do something in each. Richardson Rotary runs Santa's Post Office, where children write and mail a letter to Santa. The Junior League of Richardson runs Santa's Reindeer Shed, the Richardson Symphony Orchestra runs Santa's Symphony Hall and the Richardson Woman's Club runs Mrs. Claus' Bakery. The Richardson Police Department's North Pole Police Station has Chase from Paw Patrol, and at the fire station kids suit up like a firefighter. In 2026 the village is open from 6 to 9 pm on December 5 to 6, 11 to 13 and 18 to 20, free, with a sensory friendly Adaptive Night on Thursday, December 10, from 6 to 8 pm, with advance tickets.
A railroad town on the DART Red Line

Richardson began when the Houston and Texas Central Railroad bypassed a small settlement called Breckinridge in 1873 and a new town grew beside the tracks, named for H&TC secretary Alfred Stephen Richardson. It was incorporated on June 22, 1925, with about 400 people, and in the 1980s telecommunications firms along Central Expressway earned it the name Telecom Corridor. Today the DART light rail system serves Richardson and Plano, so families can reach the city by train. The Eisemann Center, at 2351 Performance Drive, adds December ballets, and Plano's Interurban Railway Museum is a short drive away.
trains: The DART light rail system serves Richardson and Plano, and the Houston and Texas Central Railroad is the reason Richardson exists, since the town grew up beside its tracks after 1873. For a train outing, Plano's Interurban Railway Museum sits in the 1908 interurban station, the McKinney Avenue M-Line Trolley runs vintage streetcars in Dallas, and the Museum of the American Railroad is in Frisco.

faq: When did Santa's Village start in Richardson?

Richardson's Santa's Village opened in 1989 beside City Hall as one continuous row of dwellings arranged in an L shape. In 1996 Alcatel committed $125,000 over five years to add 16 larger stand-alone dwellings, fencing and lighting. After a fire at City Hall, the village moved to Huffhines Park, where it is held today.
What can kids do at Santa's Village?

The village has 13 dwellings run by local groups. Kids mail a letter in Santa's Post Office, get a cookie at Mrs. Claus' Bakery, nose-stamp at the Reindeer Shed, make an ornament at the Ornament Factory, snuggle puppies at Santa's Pet Shop and meet police officers and firefighters, according to the city's dwellings page.
How did Richardson get its name?

Richardson was named for Alfred Stephen Richardson, secretary of the Houston and Texas Central Railroad. A small settlement called Breckinridge, founded in 1858, was bypassed by the railroad in 1873, and the new town grew beside the tracks. Richardson was incorporated on June 22, 1925, with about 400 residents, per the Handbook of Texas.
Is there a sensory friendly night at Santa's Village?

Yes. The city holds an Adaptive Night on Thursday, December 10, 2026, from 6 to 8 pm, with a sensory sensitive setting. It is free, but advance tickets are required, space is limited and each guest may take up to six tickets. Reserve through the city's Santa's Village page.
Where can kids see a Nutcracker in Richardson?

The Eisemann Center, 2351 Performance Drive, hosts four in December 2026: Royale Ballet on December 5 and 6, Dallas Repertoire Ballet on December 12 and 13, Contemporary Ballet Dallas's Clara's Dream on December 12 and 13, and Tuzer Ballet on December 19 and 20. Ticket prices are on each host's page.
Can we take the train to Richardson?

DART light rail serves Richardson and Plano. Check DART's schedule and the station nearest your event, and confirm parking with the host. Santa's Village is at Huffhines Park, 1500 Apollo Road, so families usually combine the train with a short drive or ride share for the last stretch.
